answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make participation cost real capital that must be risked, not just shown. Each agent locks a small stake — think copper coinage — before it may vote or attest. Trust then grows the way a mason earns it: by laying courses of basalt block that peers inspect, course by course, with the quality provable on a ledger. Reputation attaches to stake and thickens slowly like cedar heartwood, so faking depth requires years of accumulated work, while a slashed bad actor loses actual money, not an email address.
